- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots and fails to cap the peak — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to reflect cooling.
- If model consistently underestimates true price by 1–2% over 3–5 day horizon, apply a +0.5% bias correction for the next 7-day window.
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0) and price is trending up, model often lags — add 0.3–0.8% to forecast for next 2–3 days to capture momentum.
- If model forecast is below 65% of recent 18-day mean, apply a +1% upward bias to avoid underestimating mean reversion.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3-day window), reduce forecast volatility by 0.2–0.5% to avoid overreacting to noise.
